1995.notes: Bridged under the statute-history rule between the ACIR table for tax year 1994 (1995 ed., vol. 1, Table 19, compiled October 1994; this file's 1994 entry) and the 1997 DFA tax table (this file's 1997 entry), which print the same 1%-7% schedule (Ark. Code Ann. s. 26-51-201, not indexed before 1999) and the same 10% standard deduction with a $1,000 maximum (s. 26-51-430 before Act 328 of 1997). The Arkansas General Assembly's acts index (arkleg.state.ar.us, Acts search by range with keyword 'income tax' and with '26-51-201') lists no act of the 1995 regular session or the 1995 first extraordinary session amending s. 26-51-201 or s. 26-51-430 (the 1995 income tax acts are credits, apportionment, gross-income exclusions, IRC conformity and the Act 916 school-funding surcharge), there was no 1996 session, and the first rate and standard-deduction changes after 1994 are Act 328 of 1997 (standard deduction $2,000 from tax year 1998, CPI indexing of the brackets from 1999). The acts index was searched by keyword, so an amending act whose title omits 'income tax' or the section number would have been missed. Same schedule for single and joint returns (joint brackets not doubled; two-earner married taxpayers may file separately on the same return). Personal exemptions are tax credits ($20 per taxpayer, $40 on a joint return, $20 per dependent) and are not modelled. Low-income tax tables not modelled.

1997.notes: Statutory brackets (Ark. Code Ann. § 26-51-201), not indexed before 1999; derived from the 1997 Itemized Deduction Tax Table 3 (all 499 rows up to $49,900 reproduced exactly, tax computed at the midpoint of each $100 band). Standard deduction 10% of income up to $1,000 for single, joint and head of household (up to $500 each for status 4/5), per the 1997 AR1000 instructions (https://web.archive.org/web/20060928222150/http://www.arkansas.gov/dfa/income_tax/ind_tax/1997_forms/97-1000ip.pdf) and built into Standard Deduction Tax Table 2.
